thread:
maria: heads-up — I hit a surprising behavior in the Go SDK sampleapp: generator streaming doesn't stop when the caller cancels the ctx if an auth refresh/retry happens mid-stream.

maria: Minimal repro (trimmed):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, _ := client.Generators.Generate(ctx, req)
// background refresher may rotate token
cancel()
for ch := range stream.Chunks() {
  fmt.Println(ch) // still prints for several seconds after cancel
}
```

maria: From logs: request gets 401, refresher kicks, a retry request is sent and streaming continues despite ctx.Err() != nil.

sam: Is the refresher swapping Authorization on the transport or doing a sync refresh in the request goroutine?

maria: Sampleapp uses a RoundTripper wrapper that swaps the header when token changes. The auth retry path reconstructs an http.Request and sets the header. I suspect the rebuilt request doesn't carry the original request ctx.

john: If retry builds a new request without req.WithContext(origCtx) the cancel won't propagate — seen this pattern before.

elaine: I audited runtime/retry.go — retryAuth() does http.NewRequest + header mutation, but doesn't call WithContext. That would explain it.

sam: Short-term: ensure any retried request uses the original req.Context() (req = req.WithContext(origCtx)). Long-term: don't do blocking token refresh on the per-request goroutine.

john: Agreed. Blocking refresh in the request goroutine couples token lifecycle to request cancellation. Better to surface a retriable error and let the retry orchestrator (which owns ctx) handle refresh/retry.

maria: I'll open a small patch that: 1) attaches orig ctx to retried requests, 2) adds a unit test asserting cancel stops stream even when auth refresh is delayed, and 3) adds a short README note in generator onboarding about this gotcha.

elaine: I'll add an integration test that spins up a fake auth server which delays the refresh for a few seconds; test cancels the ctx immediately and asserts the stream loop exits promptly. Covers leak/regression.

ci-bot: buildkite: started pipeline #9010 for branch fix/attach-ctx-on-retry

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/357 — includes ctx copy on retry, the integration test, and a sampleapp README snippet recommending using context.WithTimeout for interactive flows.

sam: Nice. Add an explicit example in the generator README showing `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)` for user-facing requests; we get a lot of copies of the naive pattern.

john: Also add a short devex onboarding bullet: "Avoid inline blocking token refresh in per-request goroutines; prefer centralized refresher or reattach original ctx on retry." That will save new contributors time.

elaine: Code + tests look good, two small style nits left. Tests reproduce cancel behavior reliably in CI.

maria: Thanks — merging once CI is green. Will monitor for timing flakiness on dedicated test matrix.

sam: Good catch and clear write-up, Maria. :thumbsup:
